look.why: A fresh canopy-leaf lime that harmonizes with the olive-lime wing covers while contrasting with the glossy black horn.

size.measure: total length 5–17 cm in adult males including the long thoracic horn

habitat.text: Humid montane and lowland rainforests from southern Mexico through Central America to Bolivia and Brazil.

diet.text: Decaying wood as larvae; fermenting fallen tropical fruit and tree sap as adults.

facts.text: Males sport a giant thoracic horn longer than their body, which they use like pincers to flip rivals off tree branches.
Its wing covers change color from olive-yellow in dry air to black in high humidity due to light-refracting micro-structures.
